items.title: Mindset
items.text: Languages and AI are tools, and with development judgment and ingenuity I can work with any of them.

items.title: Before the architecture
items.text: I organize ideas and requirements before deciding the project architecture.

items.title: Failed test, rejected feature
items.text: I apply TDD to what is essential: those features are not approved until they pass their tests.

items.title: Communication
items.text: As Tech Lead I made clear communication, inside the team and with the organization, a priority.

items.title: Agile methods: sprints and tickets
items.text: I use GitHub Projects features: milestones to set deadlines and sprints, and issues as tickets or tasks to delegate and share the work across the team.

items.title: Proof: a stack nobody knew
items.text: On IMeet, leading a team of 4, we chose Python and FastAPI, outside our usual stack, to show that concepts and judgment are enough to adapt. Result: a deployed full-stack app.

imeet.title: IMeet
imeet.summary: Platform that connects mentors and students; each booking creates the Meet session automatically.
imeet.description: Final project, MigraCode bootcamp. Tech Lead of a team of 4: led the group from architecture to deployment, built the backend with Python, FastAPI and PostgreSQL, and connected it to Google Calendar and Meet so each booking creates the session automatically. Discontinued; redeployed as a demo.
imeet.role: Tech Lead of a team of 4

highlights.title: Leading the team
highlights.decision: Led a team of 4 from architecture to deployment to connect mentors and students, with React because the team already knew it.
highlights.result: Live demo, deployed on Netlify and Railway.

highlights.title: Team process
highlights.decision: Organized the work with GitHub Projects: milestones, sprints and issues as tickets, so communication inside the team and with the organization stayed clear.
highlights.result: A visible plan for the whole team: milestones, sprints and tickets in one place.

highlights.title: Backend
highlights.decision: Built the backend with Python, FastAPI and SQLAlchemy, with PostgreSQL (Supabase) for relational data, and tested it with Pytest.
highlights.result: A tested API that manages users, roles, slots and bookings.

highlights.title: A new stack
highlights.decision: Adapted Express and Node knowledge to Python and FastAPI, a stack the team chose on purpose and nobody knew.
highlights.result: A working backend for the live demo, built to show that development concepts work in any language.

highlights.title: Integrations
highlights.decision: Integrated Google sign-in and Calendar/Meet sync as optional services, for speed.
highlights.result: A booking creates the Calendar event with a Meet link automatically.

minitweet.title: Minitweet
minitweet.summary: Reddit-inspired social network with real-time comments and private chat. Installable PWA.
minitweet.description: Vue course project, Escuela Da Vinci. Solo developer: a Reddit-inspired social network with Vue and Firebase, with my own authentication and authorization system, real-time comments and private chat. Installable PWA.

highlights.title: Authentication
highlights.decision: Built a Reddit-inspired social network with Vue and Firebase (a BaaS, Backend as a Service, taught in the course), with my own authentication and authorization system.
highlights.result: Secure authorization that protects each user's posts from changes by others.

highlights.title: Real-time features
highlights.decision: Implemented CRUD of text and media posts, real-time comments and private chat.
highlights.result: Installable PWA with real-time features, deployed on Netlify.
